# Discrepancies between the formalization and the source

Source: arXiv:2009.00227 (TeX `sources/BeltranRoosSeeger2024Memoirs-arxiv.tex`).

## E1 — 2026-10-01T21:57:04-04:00 — lattice dependence of Λ*_γ (§1, eq. (eqn:maxform); §4.2)

- Source: Λ*_γ is defined as a sup over γ-sparse 𝔖 ⊂ 𝔔 for "a" dyadic lattice 𝔔, but the proof in
  §4.2 ends with sparse families in the different lattices 𝒟^{(ν)} of the Three Lattice Theorem.
  With a single fixed lattice and lattice-independent constants the bound fails (a single-scale
  averaging operator tested on two intervals adjacent to a point that is a cube boundary for many
  generations).
- Resolution: Λ*_γ is formalized as the sup over γ-sparse families contained in *any*
  Lerner–Nazarov dyadic lattice, which is the reading the §4.2 argument proves. Resolved
  (interpretation; no change to the intended theorem).

## E2 — 2026-10-01T21:57:04-04:00 — Lorentz norms (§1, (bdness-wt), (bdness-rt))

- Source: uses Hunt's normalization of the L^{p,r} norms (via f**).
- Formalization: Grafakos' quasinorms ‖f‖_{p,∞} = sup_t t d_f(t)^{1/p}, ‖f‖_{q,1} = q ∫ d_f^{1/q}.
  They are equivalent with constants depending only on p, q, so A(p), A(q) change by such factors,
  absorbed in ≲_{p,q,ε,γ,d}. Resolved (convention).

## E3 — 2026-10-01T21:57:04-04:00 — adjoint regularity (p-q-rescaled-reg-b)

- Source: a bound on (Dil_{2^j} T_j^*)∘Δ_h : L^{q'}_{B₂*} → L^{p'}_{B₁*}, presupposing an adjoint
  operator with B₁*-valued outputs.
- Formalization: the dual form |⟨(Dil_{2^j}T_j) f, Δ_h g⟩| ≤ B|h|^ε ‖f‖_p ‖g‖_{q'} for simple f, g.
  It is implied by the source hypothesis and is exactly what the proof uses (term IV₃), so the
  formal theorem is at least as strong. Resolved (convention).

## E4 — 2026-10-01T21:57:04-04:00 — proof route for Corollary 3.4 (§3.3)

- Source: proves Cor. 3.4 via Lemma 3.2 and the resolution of identity of §3.2 (Seeger–Tao), with
  the restriction ϑ < 1/p (hence ε' < min{1/p, 1/q', ε} in (eqn:defeps')).
- Formalization: direct argument — each martingale difference 𝔻_m f is a finite sum of terms
  Δ_h(·) with |h| ≲ 2^{-m}, giving ‖T𝔻_m‖ ≲ 2^{-mε} sup_h |h|^{-ε}‖TΔ_h‖; summing gives Cor. 3.4
  for every ε. Only the consequence (Tjrega)/(Tjregb) is used downstream. Resolved
  (substantive change of proof route; the statements used are unchanged or stronger).

## E5 — 2026-10-01T21:57:04-04:00 — infinite Whitney sums (§4.4)

- Source: applies S = Σ T_j to b₁ = Σ_{W∈𝒲} b_{1,W} and pairs with g₂, both infinite sums of
  simple functions, whereas the T_j are only defined on simple functions.
- Formalization: run the Calderón–Zygmund argument with a finite subfamily ℱ ⊂ 𝒲 and a remainder
  f_i 1_{Ω∖∪ℱ}, whose contribution tends to 0 as ℱ increases (using the single-scale L^p→L^q
  bounds of the finitely many T_j). All estimates of the source hold uniformly in ℱ. Resolved
  (supplied omitted detail).

## E6 — 2026-10-01T21:57:04-04:00 — the exceptional set Ω (§4.4, (Omdefs))

- Source: Ω_i = {x ∈ 3Q₀ : 𝓜_r f_i(x) > …}; intersecting with the half-open cube 3Q₀ need not give
  an open set, which the Whitney decomposition requires. Also g₁ ∈ L^∞ uses |f₁| ≤ 𝓜_p f₁ a.e.
- Formalization: Ω = {𝓜_p f₁ > c₁} ∪ {𝓜_{q'} f₂ > c₂} ∪ U₁ ∪ U₂ (no intersection with 3Q₀), where
  U_i are open sets of small measure containing {|f_i| > c_i} (outer regularity), with the
  numerical constants adjusted so that |Ω| < (1-γ)|Q₀|. The properties used later
  ((W in Q0), (upperboundsWh), (Linfty-g)) are unchanged. Resolved (minor repair).
